div.head: Norðleoda 10
div.ab: 7 þeh he geþeo, þæt he hæbbe helm 7 byrnan 7 goldfæted sweord, gif he þæt land nafaþ, he byþ ceorl swa þeah.
Et si assequatur, ut habeat loricam et galeam et deauratum gladium, si terram non habeat, tamen est siþcundes (ceorlus).
And þeah he geþeo, þæt he hæbbe helm 7 byrnan 7 golde fæted sweord, gif he þæt land nafað, he bið ceorl swa þeah.
And þeh he geþeo þæt he hæbbe helm and byrnan and gold fæted sweord, gif he þæt land nafaþ, he byþ ceorl swa þeah.
And even if he prospers so that he possesses a helmet and a coat of mail and a gold-plated sword, if he has not the land, he is a ceorl all the same.
Yet even if he prospers so that he possesses a helmet and a coat of mail and a gold-plated sword, if he does not possess the land he will still be a commoner.

Und obschon er [so weit] emporkommt (wenn er erreicht lq), dass er Helm und Panzer und ein mit Goldblech belegtes (goldbelegtes H; vergoldetes lq) Schwert besitzt, wenn (obschon Ld) er jenes Land[quantum jedoch] nicht besitzt, so bleibt er dennoch Gemeiner (ist er vom Gefolgsadel lq, später).

And even though he prospers [so far] (if he attains, lq) that he has a helmet and mail-coat and a sword plated with gold (gold-adorned, H; gilded, lq), if (though, Ld) he does not hold that [amount of] land, he remains a ceorl nevertheless (he is of the gesith-nobility, lq, later).
div.note: Liebermann compares Ine 50 (MS B); lq probably received in the 11th century the gloss ‘siþcund’ to ‘ceorl’ by mistake, and Ld followed the latter; the Quadripartitus knows both.
